keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1150-1476: the page lists twelve kingdoms by modern location: Canchis and Canas (Cusco), Collas and Lupacas (Puno), Pacajes (La Paz), Carangas and Soras (Oruro), Charcas (Chuquisaca), Quillacas, Cara-caras and Chichas (Potosí), Chuis (Sucre). Canchis and Canas are left to the Inca heartland; the Colla and Lupaca have their own dossiers; the departments stand for the rest (a generous reading, the page gives no area or boundaries).

ledger.note: 1477: the Aymara kingdoms end under the Inca. The page says they disappeared 'due to the military conquest of the Inca Empire' without a date; 1477 is the end of its span. The Aymara people page: the conquest of the Altiplano 'began later than 1438 and was well completed by 1500'; the Colla-Inca war page: the Altiplano peoples were 'only fully integrated under Huayna Capac'.

notes: One dossier for the Aymara lordships the pages give no separate dates for: Pacajes, Carangas, Soras, Charcas, Quillacas, Cara-caras, Chichas and Chuis (Canas and Canchis are named in Cusco and not drawn). The Colla Kingdom (colla-kingdom, ended 1445-1450) and the Lupaca Kingdom (lupaca-kingdom, c. 1463) have their own dossiers; the overlap of their lands with these departments is nil except the Titicaca shore. The span 1150-1477 is the article's; the page gives no capital and no area, so identity.capitals is empty. The page does not mention the Collaguas or Omasuyos. The Aymara people page and the Colla-Inca war page say the Inca conquest ran to about 1500 and under Huayna Capac, later than 1477. Cliopatria's Inca shape takes Bolivia in 1497. Chuis and Sucre are listed together on the page.
